article_manifest.title: An Irishman wrecks a military plane...
article_manifest.original_title: Un Irlandais saccage un avion militaire...
article_manifest.summary: An Irishman vandalises a US military plane: He faces ten years in prison An Irish national has been charged in New York for causing extensive damage to a US military plane parked at an airport in the west of Ireland in April. . Daithi O'Corrain had broken into a C-130H troop transport aircraft, valued at $60 million and stationed at Shannon Airport, to cause maximum damage, the Department of Justice said in a statement on Tuesday (local time).

article_manifest.title: Flow of underage children to gold mining sites: In Dédougou, “Polisi I Nisonisa” raises awareness
article_manifest.original_title: Flux des enfants mineurs vers les sites d’orpaillage : A Dédougou, « Polisi I Nisonisa » sensibilise
article_manifest.summary: Launched in March 2026 in the Bankui region, Polisi I Nisonisa, which means "the police, my neighbour" in Bwamu, is a community policing initiative that focuses on dialogue and proximity to enhance security. As part of this approach, its teams visit neighbourhoods and public places to engage with local residents about their security concerns. .

article_manifest.title: New attack in the Dosso region, in south-western Niger
article_manifest.original_title: Nouvelle attaque dans la région de Dosso, dans le sud-ouest du Niger
article_manifest.summary: In Niger, an attack took place last week in the Dioundou Department, in the Dosso region, in the south-west of the country. For the time being, no official casualty figures have been released. Published on: A visit to the bereaved families following the terrorist attacks carried out in several villages in the rural municipality of Dioundiou This is how the Nigerien news agency reported the visit on Saturday of Colonel Major Bana Alhassane, the Governor of the Dosso region, to the department of Dioundiou, which borders Nigeria.

article_manifest.title: Nigeria signs a new military agreement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad
article_manifest.original_title: Le Nigeria signe un nouvel accord militaire avec le Cameroun, le Niger et le Tchad
article_manifest.summary: A new military agreement has been concluded between Nigeria, Cameroon, Niger and Chad. It should enable Nigeria to pursue armed fighters beyond its borders. Published on: Nigeria now intends to be able to pursue armed fighters up to a distance of five kilometres into neighbouring territory .

article_manifest.title: Previous Mali: 1,505 fuel tankers in Bamako
article_manifest.original_title: Précédent Mali : 1 505 citernes de carburant à Bamako
article_manifest.summary: In total, 1,505 tanker trucks carrying petroleum products have arrived in Bamako since the beginning of November, including 840 new vehicles recently received, according to a supply report shared by several media outlets on Monday, 16 November 2026. This new delivery follows the arrival of 665 tankers on 7 November, escorted by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), against a backdrop of persistent disruptions to hydrocarbon supply chains.

article_manifest.title: Niger: A terrorist logistics base dismantled near Torodi
article_manifest.original_title: Niger : une base logistique terroriste démantelée près de Torodi
article_manifest.summary: The Nigerien army has announced that it has dismantled a logistics base belonging to armed terrorist groups near Kobagué, in the department of Torodi (Tillabéry region), in western Niger. The operation was carried out during the night of Monday 16 to Tuesday 17 November. This was a night raid led by the Torodi National Guard Squadron and the Alpha Zero Unit.

article_manifest.title: NDLEA arrests eight over cocaine shipment to Europe
article_manifest.original_title: NDLEA arrests eight over cocaine shipment to Europe
article_manifest.summary: Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have arrested eight members of a transnational drug trafficking cartel accused of moving cocaine from Lagos through Kano, Niger Republic and Libya to Europe. The suspects, who allegedly swallowed cocaine pellets to evade security checks, excreted a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilogrammes while in NDLEA custody.

article_manifest.title: Mali: Assimi Goïta equips the Army with 7 new combat and transport aircraft
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : Assimi Goïta dote l’Armée de 7 nouveaux avions de combat et de transport
article_manifest.summary: The official handover of the keys to the seven aircraft took place at the presidential pavilion of Bamako-Senou's President Modibo Keïta International Airport, in the presence of senior military officials, members of the government, the diplomatic corps and several other dignitaries. This new acquisition represents a significant strengthening of the Malian Air Force's fleet.

article_manifest.title: IP-P3A: The Coris Foundation donates 360 motorised tricycles to agricultural VDPs
article_manifest.original_title: IP-P3A : La Fondation Coris offre 360 motos tricycles aux VDP agricoles
article_manifest.summary: On Tuesday, 17 November 2026, the Coris Foundation officially handed over 360 tricycle motorcycles to the Agricultural Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDP). The formal ceremony took place at the headquarters of the National Office for Major Projects in Burkina Faso (BN-GPB). This donation will help to strengthen local production and rural logistics throughout the country.

article_manifest.title: Africa More than 68,000 Burkinabés repatriated from Guinea following measures against illegal gold mining
article_manifest.original_title: Afrique Plus de 68.000 Burkinabé rapatriés de Guinée après des mesures contre l'orpaillage illégal
article_manifest.summary: Illegal gold miners deported to Burkina Faso by Guinea-Conakry, in Bamako, on 10 November 2026. More than 68,000 Burkinabé nationals have been repatriated from Guinea since the start of operations led by Conakry against illegal gold mining, the authorities in Ouagadougou announced in a statement seen by AFP on Tuesday. .

article_manifest.title: Coup Leaders’ Promises Fall Short
article_manifest.original_title: Coup Leaders’ Promises Fall Short
article_manifest.summary: Military leaders in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger overthrew democratically elected governments, arguing that those governments had failed to suppress long-running insurgencies that junta leaders claimed they could put down. Years later, however, experts say that those juntas, like others before them, are failing their citizens in multiple ways. “A coup is not necessarily the most effective way to cure economic and political ills,” economist John Mukum Mbaku recently wrote for The Conversation.

article_manifest.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
article_manifest.title: GMS–Samé–Kati roundabout section: demolition operations launched to clear the project rights-of-way
article_manifest.original_title: Tronçon rond-point GMS–Samé–Kati : les opérations de démolition lancées pour libérer les emprises du projet
article_manifest.summary: Bamako, 17 November (AMAP) The demolition of buildings and structures located within the right-of-way of the GMS Roundabout–Samé–Kati section began on Monday, 16 November 2020, AMAP learned from an official source. The announcement was made in a joint statement by the Ministers for Transport and Infrastructure, Urban Planning, Housing, State Property, Regional Planning and Population, which was published on Sunday evening.

article_manifest.title: Niger: President Tiani makes new appointments to the senior administration
article_manifest.original_title: Niger: le Président Tiani procède à de nouvelles nominations au sein de la haute administration
article_manifest.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2020, the President of the Republic, Head of State, General Abdourahmane Tiani, signed several decrees concerning individual measures. . According to the press release issued by the Minister, Secretary General of the Government, this concerns a series of appointments to senior positions in several key ministries (Defence, Interior, Foreign Affairs, Health, Infrastructure, Transport, etc.), as well as in the central administration and at the head of public institutions.

article_manifest.title: Celebration of the 15th edition of African Road Safety Day: ANISER conducts a major roadside inspection operation in Niamey
article_manifest.original_title: Célébration de la 15è édition de la Journée Africaine de la Sécurité Routière : L’ANISER mène une vaste opération de contrôle routier à Niamey
article_manifest.summary: As part of the celebrations for the 15th edition of African Road Safety Day, the Nigerien Road Safety Agency (ANISER) organised a major road safety check operation in the city of Niamey on Sunday, 15 November 2020. . Conducted jointly with the National Police, the National Gendarmerie and the Municipal Police, this operation aims to ensure that road users, namely motorcyclists and motorists, comply with the Highway Code.

article_manifest.title: More than 68,000 Burkinabe repatriated from Guinea following measures against illegal gold mining
article_manifest.original_title: Plus de 68.000 Burkinabè rapatriés de Guinée après des mesures contre l’orpaillage illégal
article_manifest.summary: Since the beginning of November, Guinea has intensified operations against illegal gold panning, particularly in the gold-rich Siguiri region (northeast). The government accuses this activity of causing significant environmental damage and says it wants to put an end to the unregulated exploitation of mineral resources. .

article_manifest.title: Kalaban-Coura: Four people arrested after the discovery of a homemade weapon
article_manifest.original_title: Kalaban-Coura : quatre personnes interpellées après la découverte d’une arme artisanale
article_manifest.summary: Kalaban-Coura : quatre personnes interpellées après la découverte d’une arme artisanale La police de Kalaban-Coura a interpellé quatre personnes dans la nuit du 14 au 15 novembre, après la découverte d’un pistolet de fabrication artisanale. Vers 2 heures du matin, une patrouille circulait dans le quartier de Garantiguibougou. Les policiers ont remarqué deux passagers d’une moto-taxi au comportement suspect.

article_manifest.title: NDLEA arrests eight cocaine couriers, recovers 634 wraps
article_manifest.original_title: NDLEA arrests eight cocaine couriers, recovers 634 wraps
article_manifest.summary: Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency have arrested eight members of a transnational drug trafficking cartel accused of moving cocaine from Lagos through Kano, Niger Republic and Libya to Europe. The suspects, who allegedly swallowed cocaine pellets to evade security checks, excreted a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilogrammes while in NDLEA custody.

article_manifest.title: Niger: Appointment of New Secretaries General to the Ministries of Defence and the Interior
article_manifest.original_title: Niger : Nomination des nouveaux SG aux ministères de la défense et de l’intérieur
article_manifest.summary: Niamey, 17 November (ANP) – Brigadier General MAMANE SOULEY, General Officer of the Nigerien Armed Forces, has been appointed Secretary General of the Ministry of National Defence, while Colonel Major NOMA DARI has been promoted to Deputy Secretary General, according to a decree issued by the President of the Republic and made public on 16 November 2026. . At the Ministry of the Interior, Public Security and Territorial Administration, Police Commissioner General Ayouba Abdou Rahamane has been appointed Secretary General of the said ministry, according to the same source.

article_manifest.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
article_manifest.title: Nioro du Sahel: The efforts of the FAMa are helping to revive economic activity and transport
article_manifest.original_title: Nioro du Sahel : Les efforts des FAMa favorisent la reprise des activités économiques et des transports
article_manifest.summary: Nioro du Sahel, 17 November 2026 (AMAP) – The efforts of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) to improve security and facilitate the free movement of people and goods are contributing to the gradual return to normality in Nioro du Sahel. . The arrival of several dozen fuel tankers, the resumption of transport links with Bamako and Kayes, and the restocking of markets are all signs of this improvement after nine months of severe disruption.

article_manifest.title: Air Force: The fleet is gaining in heavy transport and mobility
article_manifest.original_title: Armée de l’air : la flotte gagne en transport lourd et en mobilité
article_manifest.summary: CURRENTLY From January to October 2026, the Malian Air Force carried out more than 7,000 sorties, totalling nearly 26,000 flight hours. Brigadier General Alou Boï Diarra, Chief of Staff of this component, also reported that around 28,000 passengers and more than 2,000 tonnes of cargo were transported during this period. .

article_manifest.title: Mali: The FAMa target bases and logistics depots of armed groups in Abeïbara and Sévaré
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : les FAMa ciblent des bases et dépôts logistiques de groupes armés à Abeïbara et Sévaré
article_manifest.summary: Maliweb

article_manifest.title: Customs cooperation: Nigerian trainee officers on an immersion programme in Niamey to familiarise themselves with border security strategies
article_manifest.original_title: Coopération douanière: des officiers stagiaires nigérians en immersion à Niamey pour s’imprégner des stratégies de sécurisation des frontières
article_manifest.summary: As part of the cooperation between the customs administrations of Niger and Nigeria, thirteen (13) trainee officers from the Nigerian Customs Service (NCS) will be carrying out a study visit in Niamey from 14 to 21 November 2026, in order to analyse the experience of their counterparts from the Nigerien Directorate General of Customs (DGD) in combating transnational threats.

article_manifest.title: Mali: The FAMa target bases and...
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : les FAMa ciblent des bases et...
article_manifest.summary: Mali: The FAMa target bases and logistics depots of armed groups in Abeïbara and Sévaré The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) have carried out new precision strikes against positions of armed terrorist groups in the Abeïbara and Sévaré sectors . These operations, carried out on 14 and 16 November 2026 as part of Operation Dougoukoloko, targeted assembly points housing armed individuals and military equipment, according to the General Staff of the Armed Forces.

article_manifest.title: Bamako, the new battleground for influence, or why the AFRICOM Commander visited the arms fair...
article_manifest.original_title: Bamako, nouveau terrain de la lutte d’influence, ou pourquoi le commandant de l’AFRICOM s’est rendu au salon de l’arm...
article_manifest.summary: Bamako, the new battleground for influence, or why the AFRICOM Commander visited the arms fair in Mali Russia, Türkiye and the United States are continuing their rivalry for military and political influence in the Sahel. This is what the BAMEX defence and security exhibition, which has just taken place in Mali, demonstrates. .

article_manifest.title: Mali: Nearly 80,000 people expelled from Guinea already repatriated, 13 deaths recorded
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : près de 80 000 personnes refoulées de Guinée déjà rapatriées, 13 décès enregistrés
article_manifest.summary: The Centre for Crisis Coordination and Management (CECOGEC), a Malian government body, announced on 16 November 2026 that 79,044 people deported from Guinea have already returned home, thanks to 522 vehicles, including 421 lorries and 101 coaches. Thirteen deaths were also recorded during the operations. .

article_manifest.title: Malian Armed Forces: New aircraft to dominate the skies
article_manifest.original_title: Forces armées maliennes : De nouveaux appareils pour dominer le ciel
article_manifest.summary: Our country has just taken a historic step, thereby confirming its inexorable progress towards strategic defence autonomy across the entire national territory. Yesterday, the Transitional President and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi Goïta, handed over a substantial consignment of air equipment to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). .

article_manifest.title: Niger: Police Commissioner General Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou, new Director General of the National Police
article_manifest.original_title: Niger : Le Commissaire Général de Police Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou, nouveau DG de la Police nationale
article_manifest.summary: Niamey, 17 November (ANP) – Police Commissioner General Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou, formerly Director of the Central Office for the Suppression of Illicit Drug Trafficking (OCRTIS), has been appointed Director General of the National Police (DGPN), by decree signed on 13 November by the President of the Republic, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani. . With several years of experience in the field of public safety, the new Director General of the National Police has a professional career marked by significant responsibilities in Niger and abroad.

article_manifest.title: Tahoua: Significant quantity of weapons and ammunition seized in Ibecetane
article_manifest.original_title: Tahoua : Saisie d’une importante quantité d’armes et de munitions à Ibecetane
article_manifest.summary: Tahoua, 17 November (ANP) – A large quantity of weapons and ammunition has been seized by the Niger National Guard (GNN) in Ibecetane, in the Rural Commune of Akoubounou, Abalak Department (Tahoua Region). This seizure was presented to the Governor of the Region, Colonel-Major Souleymane Amadou Moussa, on Monday, 16 November 2026, on the premises of the Tahoua Regional District of the GNN.

article_manifest.title: Air Force: Over 7,000 sorties and 26,000 flight hours completed in ten months
article_manifest.original_title: Armée de l’Air : Plus de 7 000 sorties et 26 000 heures de vol réalisées en dix mois
article_manifest.summary: The Malian Air Force carried out more than 7,000 sorties, totalling nearly 26,000 flight hours between January and October 2026. During this period, it also transported around 28,000 passengers and more than 2,000 tonnes of cargo. These figures were announced on Monday, 16 November 2026, by the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, Brigadier General Alou Boï Diarra, on the occasion of the official handover of new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa).

article_manifest.title: ORGANISED CRIME IN SIKASSO: A FAKE SOLDIER ARRESTED
article_manifest.original_title: GRAND BANDITISME À SIKASSO : UN FAUX MILITAIRE INTERPELLÉ
article_manifest.summary: An individual who was impersonating a sergeant in the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) was arrested in Sikasso in recent days for falsely claiming a title. This arrest is reminiscent of a previous case recorded in the same town in October 2024, when a bogus customs officer was arrested for (…) By Mahamane TOURE – NOUVEL HORIZON

article_manifest.title: Mali: The FAMa carry out precision strikes against terrorist groups in Abeibara and Sévaré
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : les FAMa mènent des frappes de précision contre des groupes terroristes à Abeïbara et Sévaré
article_manifest.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national public that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing their ongoing operations to monitor, control and secure the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. . On Saturday, 14 November 2026, a gathering point for armed terrorist groups, housing several individuals as well as military equipment, including vehicles and a fuel depot, was the target of precision strikes between eight (8) and ten (10) kilometres north and north-east of Abeïbara.

article_manifest.title: Mali: 13 people deported from Guinea found dead
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : 13 morts parmi les personnes refoulées de Guinée
article_manifest.summary: The deportations of Malian and Burkinabé nationals from gold mining areas in Guinea have resulted in 13 deaths in Mali, while 79,044 people have been transported as part of return operations, according to a report from the Centre for Coordination and Crisis Management (CECOGEC), published on Monday, 16 November 2026. These figures illustrate the scale of this humanitarian crisis, which has been mobilising the Malian and Burkinabé authorities, health services and aid organisations for several weeks.

article_manifest.title: Mali: 1,505 fuel tankers in Bamako
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : 1 505 citernes de carburant à Bamako
article_manifest.summary: In total, 1,505 tanker trucks carrying petroleum products have arrived in Bamako since the beginning of November, including 840 new vehicles recently received, according to a supply report shared by several media outlets on Monday, 16 November 2020. . This new arrival follows the receipt of 665 tankers on 7 November, under escort by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), in a context marked by persistent disruptions to hydrocarbon supply chains.

article_manifest.title: Mali-Russia: Seven new aircraft strengthen the military fleet
article_manifest.original_title: Mali-Russie : sept nouveaux aéronefs renforcent la flotte militaire
article_manifest.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the Malian army took delivery of seven new aircraft acquired as part of its military cooperation with Russia, comprising one strategic transport aircraft and six helicopters, intended to strengthen its mobility, logistical transport and air support capabilities. . The handover ceremony, presided over by the Head of State, Army General Assimi Goïta, took place at Bamako-Sénou's President Modibo Keïta International Airport, in the presence of several government and military officials.

article_manifest.title: Mali: Assimi Goïta hands over an Ilyushin IL-76 aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters to the Air Force
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : Assimi Goïta remet un avion Iliouchine IL-76 et des hélicoptères Mi-24 et Mi-8 à l’armée de l’air
article_manifest.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2026, the President of Mali's Transitional Government, Army General Assimi Goïta, officially handed over new aircraft to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) at Modibo Keïta-Sénou International Airport. . Comprising an IL-76 strategic transport aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters, this equipment is intended to strengthen the operational, logistical and air capabilities of the Malian army.

article_manifest.title: Mali: New military aircraft to strengthen the Army's capabilities
article_manifest.original_title: Mali : de nouveaux aéronefs militaires pour renforcer les capacités de l’Armée
article_manifest.summary: On Monday, 16 November 2020, at Président Modibo KEÏTA-Sénou International Airport, the Transitional President, Head of State and Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, Army General Assimi GOÏTA, officially handed over the keys to an Ilyushin IL-76 strategic transport aircraft and Mi-24 and Mi-8 helicopters to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). . This acquisition, funded by the State, strengthens the operational and logistical capabilities of the national defence force and reflects the commitment of the highest authorities to continue efforts to modernise the defence force.

article_manifest.title: Niger: A new Director General at the head of the DGPN
article_manifest.original_title: Niger : Un nouveau directeur général à la tête de la DGPN
article_manifest.summary: Niamey, 16 November (ANP) – On Friday, 13 November 2020, the President of the Republic, Army General Abdourahamane Tiani, signed two decrees appointing the new Director General and Deputy Director General of the National Police (DGPN). This concerns Chief Police Commissioner Aboubacar Issaka Oumarou, Service No. 50 865, appointed Head of the General Directorate of the National Police (DGPN), and Divisional Police Commissioner Abdoulaye Maman Mijinyawa, Service No.

article_manifest.title: Guinea: A government delegation from Mali visits Conakry
article_manifest.original_title: Guinée : Une délégation gouvernementale du Mali en visite à Conakry
article_manifest.summary: CONAKRY – A high-level ministerial delegation from the Republic of Mali arrived in Conakry on Tuesday, 10 November 2026. Led by the Minister of Mines, Professor Amadou Keïta, the delegation was welcomed on arrival by the Chief of Staff of Guinea's Ministry of Mines and Geology. This official visit is part of the Malian authorities' participation in the first edition of the Simandou Mining Summit, which is scheduled to open this Wednesday, 11 November, on Kassa Island, Africaguinee.com has learned from sources close to the department headed by Bouna Sylla.
